gaps.description: No general style or attribute editor in the properties panel: only what the hand-written sections expose.
The AI generator validator only keeps its tag list: anything else becomes a div or is dropped.
CSS that needs a selector (states, pseudo-elements, structural selectors): a node only holds inline declarations, so no rule can be written.

A stored event handler attribute is a string of code, so both renderers drop it on purpose (blockedNodes.ts). What closes this is a stored behaviour for the event: the behaviour model or custom code, neither of which exists yet.
The AI generator validator only keeps style keys in CSS_PROP_SET.
The palette offers five tags and the properties panel cannot change a tag, so other elements come only from the AI generator or a default page template.
Media queries beyond width: print, dark mode and reduced motion have no home.
The AI generator validator only keeps a short list of attributes.
Behaviour and state: no way to say that one element changes another.
At-rules: no way to store @keyframes, @container, @supports, @font-face and the rest.
Embedded content dropped by blockedNodes.ts (iframe, object, embed, ...), although these are ordinary content elements.
Text mixed with elements: a node holds one string or children, and the renderers drop the string.
An HTML attribute whose name is also a CSS property (width, height) is read as a style, so the editor loses the attribute: a canvas bitmap size or an image size hint is not the same as a declaration.
JSX that is a program, not markup: reported as left over by the static import, as the plan requires.

The contract passes on the published page, but the mounted editor changes the outcome: Space pans, a link does not navigate, and the editor's own main element stops a header inside it being a banner. Closing it takes an interact mode on the canvas.
A stored value a renderer refuses, overwrites or loses.
The AI generator validator keeps the property but refuses this value.
